content.comment_body: How can I use a simulator for a master-to-master network program?

Hello. I wasn’t aware this was possible, so I decided to give it a try. You can test networked modules in [product_name] V8 for [version_no]. Download the sample programs under 'MASTER-MASTER COMMUNICATION' at [url]. Open both the CLIENT and SERVER projects with [product_name], ensuring you have both programs open in the same session. Next, drag each program into the 'Network Project' section—first the SERVER, then the CLIENT. Once inside 'Network Project,' you’ll see both controllers linked with their respective programs. To link them: hold click on pin 1, drag to pin 2, and release. Double-click the new connection to configure the network mapping. Enter the values as shown, noting which device acts as server and client, then close the window. For both programs, enable simulation and select network linking. Refer to HELP in the software under 'Simulating network communication' for more details. Was this information helpful? [user_name]
Thank you very much, this was really helpful! The main thing I missed was pressing button 3B in your picture. Once I did that, I was able to simulate the network. Thanks again!
Thank you for your positive feedback. It’s a bit funny—I put so much effort into explaining it, and what you needed was just that last button. Enjoy experimenting! [user_name]

One more question: During simulation, when I trigger an input on one master device, the corresponding network input on the other is also triggered. However, when a network output is set by the program on one master, the matching output on the other doesn’t switch on. Why is the signal exchange working only in one direction, not both?

[user_name], This depends on your exchange configuration in step 2C. Even if elements are linked to memory, nothing will happen unless the exchange is included in the settings. You also need to define the direction of data flow by adjusting the arrow. Suggestion: Compress your project and share it here—someone will likely review it and offer advice. Greetings, [user_name]
I've resolved it—the exchange now works perfectly. Thanks so much!
I have another issue: I’m unable to print my program. The print icon in the file menu isn’t available. How can I activate printing?
I was able to print now. Some connectors were not assigned, which caused the print option to be unavailable. Assigning them solved the issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are able to simulate master-to-master networking with [product_name] V8. Initial issues include difficulty achieving bidirectional network signal exchange, which is fixed after setting up the network properties correctly. Problems with printing the program are solved by ensuring all connectors are assigned, enabling the printing feature.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward simulation of master-to-master communication, reliable bidirectional data exchange, and an easy way to print out programming diagrams from the software.
